nodes.title: Design tokens
nodes.role: N1 — the only node allowed to define CSS values
nodes.covenant: Design decisions are data, not code.
nodes.description: Design decisions expressed as CSS custom properties. The token generation toolchain reads the Supabase styling collections and writes the generated palette plus each target's token file; it is TypeScript today (pnpm tokens:sync, scripts/sync-tokens.ts), and a Rust CLI binary is the target. Every other node reads tokens via var() or its platform equivalent — no node above ever declares its own colour, radius, spacing or motion duration. N1 is target-agnostic: what it emits varies by target, what it guarantees does not.
implementation_rules: Define every value in :root and .dark blocks.
Register tokens in the Tailwind @theme inline block so utility classes resolve.
No hardcoded hex values, rgba(), or inline style={{}} outside N1.
Category-to-mineral mapping lives here, not in components.

nodes.title: Primitives
nodes.role: N2 — smallest composable unit of UI
nodes.covenant: A primitive does one thing well.
nodes.description: The smallest composable unit of UI, and framework-specific by nature: a primitive is a contract plus a token set, not one source file shared across targets. Shipping today are React (the verified Mzizi baseline) and Svelte via shadcn-svelte, both Radix + CVA — Svelte is a supported way to build a primitive, no longer the primary one. The Rust path is Dioxus, whose 0.7 Tailwind + Radix support matches this exact stack; it is metadata_only today, with zero Dioxus primitives wired. Target: primitives read accessibility state and motion config from the shared Rust WASM core. No harness and no business logic here — the harness stays N3-only.
implementation_rules: One CVA variants block per primitive; no inline conditional classes.
Expose asChild / Slot where composition matters.
Use Radix UI for focus, keyboard, and screen-reader behaviour.
56px default / 48px minimum touch target.

nodes.title: Brand components
nodes.covenant: A brand component is a primitive with Ubuntu in it.
nodes.description: Primitives wrapped in Ubuntu philosophy. Brand components consume the harness for observability, motion and accessibility — every one destructures { log, motion, LiveRegion } from it, and N2 primitives never do. The harness is TypeScript today (lib/harness in nyuchi/mzizi); the target is one shared Rust WASM core behind that same interface, so the harness is implemented once instead of once per framework. The component shell stays framework-specific either way: Dioxus on the Rust path, Svelte optional, Swift / Kotlin / ArkTS / React Native idiomatic native.
implementation_rules: Always destructure { log, motion, LiveRegion } from useNyuchiHarness.
N2 primitives never import useNyuchiHarness directly.
Every brand component carries a data-slot attribute for stable targeting.
Use mineral palette tokens, not raw colour values.

nodes.title: Safety rails
nodes.role: N4 — input validation, output sanitisation, AI guardrails
nodes.description: Validation, sanitisation and AI guardrails. TypeScript today — Zod schemas at the entry point and the ai-safety lib wrapping completions. Target: the gate logic (permission evaluation, content moderation, wallet state, trust-score validation) compiles to WebAssembly via wasm-bindgen for the browser and to a native binary for server-side API validation, with a thin framework shell rendering the visual gate — verification-required screens, blocked states — by reading state from the module. This is Rust-as-shared-core, not Rust-as-UI: one of the two nodes with a genuine Rust implementation, because a safety gate is logic and logic does not need rewriting per target.
implementation_rules: Validate all external input with Zod schemas at the entry point.
Sanitise every rich-text or MDX payload before render.
Wrap AI completions with the ai-safety lib (see registry:lib).
Treat every third-party response as untrusted until it clears N4.

nodes.title: Resilience patterns
nodes.role: N5 — circuit breakers, retries, timeouts, fallback chains
nodes.covenant: Failure in one part never breaks the whole.
nodes.description: Circuit breakers, retry logic, error boundaries and fallback chains. TypeScript today — circuit-breaker, retry, timeout, fallback-chain, bulkhead, rate-limiter and chaos live in lib/ and ship as registry:lib items consumers install. Target: the resilience STATE MACHINE (circuit state closed/open/half-open, failure counts, timeout budgets) is Rust compiled to WebAssembly via wasm-bindgen, while framework components render the visual fallback — error cards, skeletons, offline banners — by reading state from the module. This is Rust-as-shared-core, not Rust-as-UI: alongside N4 it is one of the two nodes with a genuine Rust implementation, because both hold logic rather than UI. The isolation is the point and it is genuine: a UI failure cannot corrupt resilience state, and a state transition cannot block the UI thread.
implementation_rules: Wrap every async boundary in SectionErrorBoundary.
Use the resilience lib primitives: circuit-breaker, retry, timeout, fallback-chain, bulkhead, rate-limiter.
No global error handler swallows section-level failures silently.
Chaos tests exercise the resilience paths before every release.

nodes.title: Pages
nodes.role: N6 — composition of N2 and N3, nothing implemented
nodes.covenant: A page is a composition, not an implementation.
nodes.description: Pure composition of N2 and N3 — pages arrange brand components into full-screen experiences and implement nothing. That covenant is exactly what makes N6 the cheapest node in the helix to move across targets: porting a page re-expresses an arrangement, it does not re-derive behaviour. Framework-specific like every UI node — Dioxus on the Rust path, Svelte optional, React shipping — with no Rust implementation of its own, because there is nothing here to implement. Semantic tokens only, no inline primitives.
implementation_rules: Pages import from N2 and N3, never define new primitives.
All copy, data, and metadata come from the database or props — not hardcoded.
Pages can be server components by default; promote to client only when hooks are required.
A node that renders a spinner or a skeleton pulls it from N2, never inlines one.

nodes.title: Shell
nodes.role: N7 — the app chrome: header, footer, navigation, theme
nodes.description: The app chrome — navigation, routing, theme provision and global overlays, mounted once per app. N7 is the one node that is both things at once: as UI it is framework-specific and has a Rust alternative (Dioxus on the Rust path, Svelte optional, SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose / ArkTS / React Native native), and as the mount point it is where the shared Rust WASM core is initialised once per app and its state — N4's gates, N5's resilience — made available to the component tree. TypeScript today (app/layout.tsx plus next-themes), initialising nothing from WASM.
implementation_rules: One <Header /> + one <Footer /> per app — the shell is singular.
Shell components are the only place sticky positioning, backdrop blur, and theme-provider wiring live.
The shell surfaces authentication state but never implements auth logic.
Responsive by default across every breakpoint from 320px to ultra-wide.

nodes.title: Assurance
nodes.role: N8 — observability, health monitoring, SLO tracking
nodes.covenant: What breaks is seen before users feel it.
nodes.description: The node that watches, on the engineering backbone's core-guarantee strand. Observability signal collection, SLO tracking, chaos injection, accessibility auditing and conformity checking. TypeScript today (lib/observability.ts and lib/metrics.ts in nyuchi/mzizi). Target: the collection layer compiles to WebAssembly so the browser gathers signals without blocking the UI thread, and the same Rust builds as a native binary aggregating signals across the fleet server-side. Writes to observability_events and fundi_issues. Never stores PII — in any language. Rate-limited at the application layer.
implementation_rules: Every brand component emits render timing + error events via the harness.
Structured logs use the [mzizi] prefix for grep-ability.
MCP / API usage flows into lib/metrics.ts.
Health signals are exposed at /api/v1/health; assurance dashboards read from there.

rungs.title: Fundi
rungs.role: N9 — the self-healing rung: consumes N8 assurance signals and remediates the root cause
rungs.covenant: Failure is a learning event, not a user-facing incident.
rungs.description: The self-healing rung — a cross-cutting base pair that bridges both backbones. A Cloudflare Worker at fundi.nyuchi.dev, TypeScript today (fundi-tester in nyuchi/mzizi-tools: a FundiAgent durable object, a */5 cron and the fundi-signals queue); a workers-rs Rust/WASM Worker is the target. NOT a Supabase Edge Function — fundi runs independently of the database vendor on Cloudflare's global edge. Triggered by Cron Triggers and Cloudflare Queues pushed by N8 signals. Reads observability_events and fundi_issues from Supabase via REST API, classifies failure severity, deduplicates against open GitHub issues, and creates structured issues with fundi:node/{n} labels for human review. Never auto-merges fixes. Logs every healing action append-only.
implementation_rules: The fundi worker route POST /webhook ingests and deduplicates incoming failures, authenticated by an X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC over the raw body. It replaced the fundi-webhook Supabase edge function, which had no signature check.
Cron-driven heal pass promotes fingerprinted failures into labelled GitHub issues.
Append-only audit trail in fundi_healing_log, surfaced by get_healing_log; fundi_issues holds the issues themselves.
On by default for nyuchi / mukoko; opt-in for external consumers.

rungs.title: Documentation
rungs.role: N10 — the ecosystem documents itself in code
rungs.covenant: Every document lives here. Documents, instructions, docs, documentation — one rung, no exceptions.
rungs.description: The doctrine rung, and the single home for everything document-shaped: documents, instructions (including ai_instructions), docs and documentation. Conventions, covenants, guides and reference all belong to N10 — held as MDX in the repo so a document referencing something that no longer exists fails the build rather than rotting unnoticed. If an artifact is prose meant to be read, it is N10; nothing else claims it and no other rung should.
implementation_rules: Long-form guides live in the Starlight repos: bundu-docs serves docs.bundu.org (product) and nyuchi-docs serves docs.nyuchi.com (engineering). /api/v1/docs* returns HTTP 410 with a migrated_to map.
Component source lives in git under components/registry/n<N>-<label>/; Supabase holds only the metadata around it, served over /api/v1/*.
registry.json is a CI-verified snapshot of the registry, never hand-edited (pnpm registry:verify).
MCP tools and /api/v1/stats surface live counts from the DB; never quote a hardcoded count.

rungs.title: Discovery
rungs.role: N11 — SEO + AIO: preview images, structured data, agent-readiness; entwined through the double helix, not an outside actor
rungs.covenant: If the machine can't see it, it doesn't exist.
rungs.description: Search-engine and AI/agent optimisation — the machine-facing surface of every site. Owns social/preview images, structured data (schema.org JSON-LD), llms.txt, robots + sitemap, canonical and meta tags, and agent-readiness (MCP server-card, .well-known). N11 has no Rust implementation and no Rust alternative of its own: it holds no shared logic and no components, and rides whatever the shell renders. What it does hold is a constraint on the Rust direction — a client-rendered WASM target must prerender or server-render, or crawlers receive an empty document. A missing preview image or absent structured data is the biggest discoverability no-go: if crawlers, social scrapers and AI agents cannot parse a surface, it may as well not exist.
implementation_rules: Every route ships a title, a meta description, and a dynamic OpenGraph/preview image carrying that page's title + description + site icon — never a missing or 404 image.
Preview images come from ONE shared template so they stay dynamic and brand-agnostic; the site icon parameterises the brand (nyuchi / mukoko / bundu / shamwari).
Emit schema.org JSON-LD for the page's primary entity; keep llms.txt and the MCP server-card current.
robots.txt and sitemap.xml are generated, not hand-maintained; canonical URLs are absolute via a set metadataBase.

rungs.title: Skills
rungs.role: N12 — the skills rung: what the system knows how to do, authored in git and projected to the registry
rungs.covenant: What the system knows how to do is teachable, not tribal.
rungs.description: The skills rung. Agent skills are authored in git (mzizi-tools/mzizi-skills, published as @nyuchi/mzizi-skills) and projected into the `skills` collection, which the registry serves at /api/v1/skills* and the MCP serves as get_skill / list_skills. A rung rather than a node: skills bridge both backbones — engineering practice and meaning at once — and no node imports them.
implementation_rules: Skills are authored in git as mzizi-skills/skills/<name>/SKILL.md in nyuchi/mzizi-tools and published as the public npm package @nyuchi/mzizi-skills.
pnpm skills:validate is the offline pre-publish gate: index.json and package.json version lockstep, frontmatter name matching the index, no unlisted skill directory.
pnpm skills:sync projects the committed bundle into this collection through RLS (disk to DB). The DB rows are a read-only projection; git is the source of truth.
mzizi.dev serves skills at /api/v1/skills* and over MCP; consumers install with npx skills add @nyuchi/mzizi-skills.

strands.name: core-guarantee
strands.title: Core guarantee
strands.description: The fixed contract — accessibility, data, resilience, observability, safety, and primitives. Every adopter, on any framework, with any visual identity, gets these unchanged; they are not configurable because they are the reason to trust Mzizi at all. An accessibility layer you can turn off is a suggestion, not a guarantee.

strands.name: shipped
strands.title: Shipped
strands.covenant: In the box, but free to evolve.
strands.description: Nyuchi-authored components that come in the box — brand, pages, shell. Part of the framework (not app code), but unlike the core they carry no permanence promise: they evolve at product speed.

strands.name: swappable
strands.title: Swappable
strands.covenant: Fork along the seams, not everywhere.
strands.description: The only defined fork seams — styling/tokens, the icon library, and the framework (React today, SvelteKit the declared migration target). An adopter swaps exactly these three layers and inherits everything else — forkable along seams, not forkable everywhere.

strands.name: spine
strands.title: Spine
strands.covenant: What makes the parts one body.
strands.description: The harness — the pre-wiring backbone. Not a styling layer; a structural one. The spine holds the bindings between components and their conventions, the way the sugar-phosphate backbone holds the bases: it is what makes the strands one framework instead of a parts list.

strands.name: genetic-code
strands.title: Genetic code
strands.covenant: The sequence everything is read from.
strands.description: The Ubuntu principles and Bundu conventions — the sequence everything else is read from. Not documentation about the framework; instruction to it: the five Ubuntu questions, the naming conventions, the mathematical pattern language (why sizes are primes, why sets come in sevens), and Schema.org compliance.

strands.name: transcription
strands.title: Transcription
strands.covenant: Doctrine is data, not tribal knowledge.
strands.description: Every piece of doctrine, every convention, every architectural decision stored as queryable documents in mzizi_db (component_documents) and served by the MCP. Doctrine is not tribal knowledge; it is versioned data with an audit trail that both humans and AI coding assistants query.
